history.content: i dont even know why im opening this. just had another thing with my sister and im so done
It sounds like you’re really fed up after something with your sister. What part of this feels loudest right now — anger, hurt, or just feeling done?
anger mostly. like im actually shaking. she texted the family group chat saying ill 'obviously' host christmas again bc i dont have kids so i have the time. didnt even ask me
Yeah, that sounds like a pretty sharp kind of anger — almost like your body is braced for it too. Does it feel more like wanting to push back, or more like being blocked and disrespected?

disrespected. thats the word. its like my time isnt real to them. i work full time too?? but bc theres no kids in my house everyone just assumes im free labour. this happens every single year and im sick of being the default

That sounds deeply disrespectful — like your time gets treated as less real, and you’re pushed into being the default every year. It makes sense that this keeps landing as anger; does it feel mostly like protest, or more like resentment now?

resentment honestly. been building for years. and the worst part is i KNOW if i say no theyll act like im the difficult one. my mum will do the whole 'oh dont start' thing and suddenly im the problem for not wanting to cook for 14 people again

That sounds like resentment with a lot of pressure around it — like saying no would get turned back on you. Does it feel more tight and braced, or more like you want to pull away and not deal with them at all?
pull away. i kind of just want to leave the group chat and not reply at all. let them figure it out for once. but i wont. i never do. thats the bit that makes me maddest, that i already know ill cave

That sounds like resentment that’s turned into wanting to pull away, with a really familiar trap underneath: knowing you’ll cave. We can leave it here if you want, or stay with what makes that part so maddening.
yeah lets leave it. i dont have an answer for that yet. but it actually helped to say it out loud. thanks. gonna sit with it for a bit
Of course — I’m glad saying it out loud helped a bit. I’ll leave it here with you, and if you want to come back to it later, we can.
